item.title: El-Sayed dares GOP rival to no-pads football showdown as Senate feud turns personal
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed challenged Mike Rogers to a no-pads football tackle after Rogers attacked his past comments on toxic masculinity in sports culture.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed recently escalated his feud with Republican nominee Mike Rogers, who is more than twenty years his senior, challenging the former FBI agent to a bout of tackle football after accusing Rogers of being "too afraid" to debate him.

"Since you’re too afraid to debate me, how about you ‘hold me accountable’ on a football field instead," El-Sayed posted to X on Wednesday. "Tackle, no pads like we used to play when we were kids. I’d be happy to show you [how] much I love football."

Rogers is 63 while El-Sayed is 41.

The unusual challenge comes as Rogers seeks to turn El-Sayed’s past criticism of football culture into a campaign liability, while El-Sayed has increasingly leaned into sports, fitness and a defense of masculinity as he courts male voters. The exchange quickly became personal, with Rogers’ campaign mocking El-Sayed’s height rather than accepting the challenge.

MICHIGAN DEM SENATE NOMINEE COMES UNDER FIRE OVER RESURFACED BLOG POST LINKING FOOTBALL TO 'TOXIC MASCULINITY'

El-Sayed’s X post was in response to a clip of Rogers criticizing him for past comments he made on topics such as football and the 4th of July.

"This guy spent hours hating on what most Michiganders would enjoy in their pastimes, and he should be held to account for that," Rogers said on Fox News. "These are views that he held, that he was pretty strong about, but he knew that he had to delete them all … if people really knew who he was, they wouldn’t vote for him."

In an October 2021 essay, El-Sayed wrote that "the toxic masculinity at the heart of America’s most popular sport — and men’s sports culture more generally — is way deeper than a few emails or a Jay-Z turnaround."

EL-SAYED'S THREAT AGAINST GOP RIVAL BACKFIRES AS CONSERVATIVES BRING RECEIPTS: 'IS DUBAI IN FLORIDA?'

Though some have argued that this is evidence of El-Sayed hating football, the Democratic Senate hopeful played football growing up and was the captain of his high school team. He called sports his "lifeline."

While El-Sayed has sharply criticized toxic elements of male sports culture, he has also defended masculinity and chided Democrats for talking down to men, often posting fitness-related content as part of his strategy to appeal to male voters.

Rogers’ campaign fired back at El-Sayed’s post by mocking his height.

"That’s an awfully tall threat coming from down there," the Mike Rogers War Room X account posted.

‘DOCTOR’ EL-SAYED’S BIZARRE HEALTH HUSTLE RAISES CAMPAIGN HEADACHE: ‘MOON JUICE BRAIN DUST’

Rogers’ official campaign account posted a GIF of Will Ferrell saying "he’s an angry elf" in response to El-Sayed's challenge.

El-Sayed was listed at 5 feet 9 inches during his University of Michigan lacrosse career. A 2008 news clipping, however, listed him at 5 feet 8 inches.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

item.title: Jeffrey Dean Morgan nearly quit acting after miserable ‘Star Trek’ experience: ‘I hated it so much’
item.description: Jeffrey Dean Morgan says his Xindi alien role on "Star Trek: Enterprise" nearly ended his career due to claustrophobia from 14-hour prosthetics sessions.
item.content:encoded:
Jeffrey Dean Morgan's miserable experience playing an alien on "Star Trek: Enterprise" nearly convinced him to quit acting for good.

Long before his breakout roles on "Supernatural" and "Grey's Anatomy," Morgan appeared as a Xindi alien named Damron on the sci-fi series — a job that required extensive prosthetics and left the actor struggling with claustrophobia.

"I hated it so much," Morgan recalled during an appearance on Josh Horowitz's "Happy Sad Confused" podcast. "I was like, 'That's it. I've got to do something else.'"

WILLIAM SHATNER SAYS HE'S 'TAKING CARE OF BUSINESS' AT 95: 'THE LEAST OF ALL I WANT DO IS DIE'

Morgan said he sometimes spent 14 hours a day in the prosthetics and had difficulty eating while wearing them.

"I remember I was so claustrophobic," he said. "It just was an experience that I want to forget, and I still wake up sweating about it."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

The experience came during an already tricky period in Morgan's career.

By his mid-30s, he had spent years bouncing between guest appearances, pilots and smaller movies while taking side jobs to pay his bills.

"I was always, always side hustling," Morgan said, recalling that he would build fences and take other jobs that "usually involved hammers."

NICKI MINAJ, ANNA NICOLE SMITH AND MORE STARS WHO GOT THEIR START WAITING TABLES AT RED LOBSTER

Walking away from Hollywood, however, presented its own problem.

"I was like, done, but at the same time I was like, 'What am I going to do?'" Morgan said. "I don't know anything else."

LIKE WHAT YOU’RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Morgan said he had reached his mid-30s without an education or an obvious backup career and had begun to believe acting simply wasn't going to work out.

His longtime manager then dropped him, telling him, "You've aged out, bro."

But Morgan's fortunes soon changed dramatically. 

Around age 38, he landed roles on "Supernatural," "Grey's Anatomy" and "Weeds" within roughly the same period — finally getting his breakthrough after years of struggling to stay in the business.

These days, Morgan is still going strong. 

He currently stars as Negan opposite Lauren Cohan's Maggie in the third season of AMC's "The Walking Dead: Dead City," which premiered July 26. Morgan is also an executive producer on the series.

item.title: Son of Florida alligator attack victim says tourists and TikTokers are emboldening the gators
item.description: Dina Spann's son blames tourists and TikTokers for feeding alligators on the Silver River, saying the reptiles have lost their natural fear of humans.
item.content:encoded:
The son of a Florida woman who lost part of her arm in a terrifying alligator attack is blaming tourists and TikTokers for teaching the reptiles to get a little too comfortable around humans.

Dina Spann, 58, was attacked Saturday while floating in the Silver River in Marion County. Her son, Zach Guerrina, told the New York Post that he believes people feeding, touching and otherwise getting too close to alligators are causing them to lose their natural fear of humans.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK

"Growing up in Florida, that has never been a thing. I’m in the water all the time and I’ve never had a gator want to approach," Guerrina said. "We’ve got a lot of tourists down here and a lot of people that’s moved to Florida that’s never seen an alligator before.

"There’s literally videos of people petting alligators. When you do that, these things lose fear of humans and if it gets close enough to you, it’s gonna bite you."

Guerrina said he has been visiting the Silver River since childhood and his family has floated there "hundreds of times" without incident. Since his mother's attack, however, he said he has been made aware of TikTok videos showing visitors getting dangerously close to alligators while kayaking on the river.

"It’s going to happen again out there, because if they’re feeding them like that, they’re going to come up to you," he said.

Spann was swimming in a prohibited area when the alligator attacked. The animal grabbed her right arm and pulled her underwater after she attempted to fend it off with a paddle.

Nearby boater John Gamache was eating lunch with his father when he heard the commotion and raced toward the swimmers.

"I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers," Gamache previously told Fox 35 Orlando.

The approaching boat scared the alligator away, but Spann had suffered catastrophic injuries.

"It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere. Obviously, the minutes mattered," Gamache said.

Gamache used rope from his boat to tie off Spann's injured arm while his father helped bring the other swimmers onto the boat. They then rushed the group toward a nearby launch, where first responders took over.

BOATER SCARED OFF ALLIGATOR THEN USED ROPE TO STOP BLEEDING AFTER FLORIDA WOMAN LOST ARM

Spann survived but ultimately had her right arm amputated below the elbow and also lost at least one finger on her left hand, according to Guerrina.

Her son said she has remained in "good spirits" despite the ordeal and described his mother as a "hippie soul" who loves animals and traveling. He said she had recently returned from a trip to Africa before the attack.

Guerrina also believes Florida should allow more alligators to be hunted.

"There’s too many gators out here," he told the Post. "We’ve got three people that’s been bit these last weeks –– a kid lost his hand, a girl died and now this.

"I’m not saying eradicate gators but if you’re going to put them somewhere, put them in the marsh.

"If you’re in spring water, you shouldn’t have to be concerned about an alligator."

The attack comes less than two months after 11-year-old Brodie Terry of Pennsylvania lost his hand when an 8-foot, 7-inch alligator attacked him during a June fishing trip in Marion County.

And just one day later, on June 28, another Florida alligator attack turned deadly.

Brittany Clark, 31, was hiking with her boyfriend and best friend at Little Big Eco State Forest near Orlando when the group waded into the Econlockhatchee River to cool off.

They were kneeling in roughly three feet of water when a massive alligator attacked Clark and bit both of her arms. One arm was severed and the other was nearly torn off as her boyfriend fought to free her from the animal.

Clark died before rescue workers could get her to a hospital.

Following Spann's attack, trappers contracted by the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission caught and removed a 9-foot, 8-inch alligator from the Silver River on Sunday. The river was then reopened to the public.

item.title: Marco Rubio addresses UAP government cover-up allegations, says Trump would give a speech if admin knew more
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump would hold a primetime address and would be showing UAP pictures and videos if the government had more information on the topic.
item.content:encoded:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that President Donald Trump would be showing pictures and videos of unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP) and would likely hold a primetime address if the administration knew about it, addressing how some people think the government is covering it up.

Katie Miller, host of "The Katie Miller Podcast," asked Rubio in an interview about a conspiracy theory he believed in, and he brought up UAPs, but clarified he didn't think it was a conspiracy theory.

Rubio discussed how he's been interested in UAPs ever since he was in the Senate, and said, "I don't know who it is. I don't know what it is, but there are things flying over our military installations, and they're not ours, and we should look into this, be serious about it."

UNKNOWN MILITARY AIRCRAFT CAUGHT ON VIDEO NEAR WICHITA, KANSAS BASE SPARKS B-21 RAIDER SPECULATION

"So, I don't call it a conspiracy. I don't know if I, I don't know the answer to any of it. I'm just, you know, asking the questions about, we should know what's flying over our airspace. But I don't think that's a conspiracy theory as much as it is just — it can be in some sense, because people do believe we're covering something up. And I assure you, like in this administration, if we knew, like, the president would be all over. Like there would be a primetime address. He would, he'd be showing the pictures and the videos," Rubio said.

NEW TRUMP UFO FILE DUMP INCLUDES MILITARY FOOTAGE OF MYSTERIOUS STAR-SHAPED OBJECT

The Pentagon has released several UAP videos in 2026.

"President Trump directed the Department of War to identify and release government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena, and unidentified flying objects because he is the most transparent president in history. While past administrations have sought to discredit or dissuade the American people, the President is focused on providing maximum disclosure to the public, who can ultimately make up their own minds about the information contained in these files. The American people asked, and President Trump delivered," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Fox News Digital in a statement.

The Secretary of State also conceded he used to use UAPs as a diversion tactic while speaking to reporters, but said the topic was nonetheless very serious.

"I did that for a long time in the Senate… It was extraordinarily effective as a diversionary tactic. In addition to – now, that said, it's also a very legitimate topic that we should be covering," he added.

UFO WHISTLEBLOWER CLAIMS BILLIONS IN SECRET SPENDING HIDDEN FROM CONGRESS

President Donald Trump directed federal agencies to waive prior nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) for former government employees and contractors cooperating with unidentified anomalous phenomena investigations, Fox News Digital reported in July.

"President Trump recently directed the Department of War and the intelligence community to allow former government employees or contractors that have relevant information about the disclosure of UAP, to come forward to meet with designated government representatives — AARO or the President’s UAP taskforce, ‘PURSUE’ — and have their prior NDAs abrogated," a senior administration official said, with AARO referring to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, the Pentagon office established to investigate UFOs and other unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAPs).

Another senior administration official emphasized the move was not a "declassification directive" and only allowed employees to come forward through government channels.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Officials say years of congressional inquiries, whistleblower allegations and newly declassified records have raised questions about whether additional witnesses have remained silent because they believed prior nondisclosure agreements prevented them from cooperating with government investigations.

Lead UFO Investigator for Gaia and host of "Cosmic Disclosure" Joshua Golembeske told Fox News Digital in a statement that Rubio was a big reason the UAP report existed, citing his work on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

He criticized Rubio's "diversionary tactic" remarks, and said it was "funny," but that it was the exact thing the Secretary of State was trying to fix.

"This is the same guy who spent years saying the stigma is the problem, that guys won't report what they see because they'll get laughed at. And now the Secretary of State is on a podcast saying he used it to change the subject. Pilots hear that. Witnesses hear that. That's the exact thing he was trying to fix," he said.

"Where he says if we knew, Trump would be on primetime showing the pictures. Maybe. But that assumes he'd be told. [Intelligence whistleblower David] Grusch testified under oath that these programs were kept from Congress — kept from AARO, the office we built to look into it. Rubio himself said whistleblowers came to him scared of retaliation. So 'I wasn't briefed' doesn't mean there's nothing there. It might just mean the compartment did its job," Golembeske added.

Fox News' Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

item.title: Tlaib under fire for working to unseat two Jewish House Democrats in Florida: 'No coincidence'
item.description: Rashida Tlaib is rallying in Fort Lauderdale to back socialists challenging Jared Moskowitz and Debbie Wasserman Schultz in their primaries.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., is being criticized by Florida's lone Jewish Republican in Congress as she works to unseat two fellow House Democrats.

Tlaib is appearing at a rally in Fort Lauderdale Friday held by left-wing groups in support of three congressional candidates, according to a flier posted on Instagram, including two socialists running to unseat Reps. Jared Moskowitz, D-Fla., and Debbie Wasserman Schultz, D-Fla.

"I think that it's no coincidence that she's coming to target two of the remaining Jewish Democrats," Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., told Fox News Digital.

JEFFRIES DECLINES TO BACK WASSERMAN SCHULTZ AS BLACK LEADERS REVOLT OVER DISTRICT SWITCH

"It won't be well received in Florida," he continued. "How it's received in a Democratic primary — look, the Democrats are lost. But I'm going to hope that Florida Democrats are smarter than national Democrats because the Jew hatred side of the Democratic Party is not good for America."

Tlaib has been a power player on the far left so far this election cycle as candidates linked to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) dominate establishment Democrats in key elections across the country.

But DSA-linked candidates have also been accused of criticism against Israel that approaches antisemitism, according to the group's opponents, while being sympathetic to terror groups like Hamas.

Tlaib, the first Palestinian American woman in Congress, has faced bipartisan criticism for her comments on Israel and Jewish people. The Michigan congresswoman has denied accusations of antisemitism.

FORMER BERNIE SANDERS OFFICIAL ACCUSES SENATOR OF PUSHING MOST ANTISEMITIC CANDIDATES 'IN A GENERATION'

But Fine said Tlaib was a "vocal supporter of Hamas" and said the far left was making Jews in America feel unsafe.

"I think the Democratic Party is lost, and I think it's dangerous. I don't know that it's lost and dangerous in Fort Lauderdale or Florida, but nationally, the kinds of people that the Democrats are nominating, these are people who do not love America," Fine said of the far-left surge.

"They hate it. They are here to destroy it, and no one embodies that better than Rashida Tlaib."

DSA-linked candidates have already toppled House Democrats in New York, Colorado and Michigan. Also in Michigan, socialist politician Abdul El-Sayed defeated establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens for the party's nomination for Senate.

DEMS' LEFTWARD LURCH GETS LEGS AS EL-SAYED'S MICHIGAN SENATE VICTORY SPARKS PARTY DEBATE

Tlaib campaigned with El-Sayed and other DSA candidates across the U.S.

Friday's rally is called Chomp the Oligarchy and is being hosted by progressive groups like Gen Z For Change and Florida Youth Justice Coalition.

Moskowitz and Wasserman Schultz's campaigns did not respond to requests for comment on Tlaib's appearance. Tlaib's campaign did not respond to a request for comment on Fine's remarks.

Tlaib and other Democrats have previously accused Fine of anti-Muslim racism.

Moskowitz, who represents Florida's 23rd Congressional District, is running for re-election in the 25th Congressional District, which was recently redrawn to give Republicans a better shot in the general race.

Wasserman Schultz is running in the newly redrawn 20th Congressional District, a majority-Black district that leans heavily Democratic, sparking backlash for potentially impacting the area's historically Black representation.

item.title: Trump says Karoline Leavitt will leave White House press secretary role, become outside advisor
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family, President Donald Trump announced.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump announced that White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her role at the end of the month to spend more time with her family.

Leavitt confirmed her departure in a lengthy post on X, saying she made the "bittersweet decision" after concluding she could not balance the demands of serving as press secretary with being the mother she wants to be to her two young children.

"Serving as the White House Press Secretary over the past year and a half has been the honor and adventure of a lifetime," Leavitt wrote.

Leavitt thanked Trump for giving her the opportunity to work in the West Wing, travel and represent his administration from the White House briefing room.

LEAVITT VOWS TRUMP WILL DELIVER 'ENTERTAINING' SPEECH AT HIS RETURN TO WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER

"Most of all, I am thankful to the President for entrusting me with the distinct privilege of speaking on his behalf at the White House podium. I have spoken with great pride about the many historic accomplishments of this Administration, and I have relished holding the liberal media accountable and ensuring the American people hear the truth about President Trump’s successes."

Leavitt said becoming a mother again while holding one of the White House's most demanding public-facing jobs ultimately drove her decision to leave.

"Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least. The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life."

LEAVITT RIPS BLUE STATE’S EXPLOSIVE NONCITIZEN VOTER-ROLL ADMISSION: ‘NOT A COINCIDENCE’

Leavitt said she will remain involved with Trump and Republican politics after leaving the White House.

"President Trump has asked me to continue serving as a top advisor to him on the outside, and I will always remain a vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party."

She also made clear that she plans to remain politically active.

"My fight is entering a new phase, but it is far from over."

KAROLINE LEAVITT ANNOUNCES BIRTH OF SECOND CHILD, A GIRL

Leavitt, 28, became the youngest White House press secretary in history when Trump returned to office in January 2025. She previously served as national press secretary for Trump's 2024 presidential campaign and worked in the White House press office during his first administration.

Leavitt recently returned to the White House after taking leave following the birth of her second child, a daughter, in May.

Trump separately praised Leavitt in announcing her departure, calling her one of his most trusted aides and saying she would become one of his top outside advisors.

"Our wonderful White House Press Secretary, and one of my most trusted aides, Karoline Leavitt, will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect!" Trump said.

"Karoline will now be one of my top outside advisors, and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections."

Trump praised Leavitt's work in the White House and on his political campaigns.

"Karoline has been a real leader in the White House, and has done a phenomenal job fighting for Justice, Liberty, and Freedom, since 2018, including our Historic Re-Election Campaign of 2024. Karoline has been one of the best White House Press Secretaries in the History of the Office. Thank you, Karoline, for a job well done!"

Trump did not immediately name a successor to Leavitt as White House press secretary.

item.title: Cowboys WAG Haley Cavinder fires back at a nasty troll, Pat McAfee triggers the mob & Seahawks coach loses it!
item.description: Haley Cavinder fires back at an internet troll who mocked her looks, while Pat McAfee faces backlash for sitting with Trump at a high school event.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday–Friday on OutKick.com.

Second Hump Day of August. We're here. We've made it. We've all waited for this day. We've grinded our tails off for MONTHS now for this very moment ... NFL Preseason Week 1 Eve! Can you feel it? Who's excited? Anyone? Bueller?

Fine. It ain't exactly the real thing, but Lord knows it beats more WNBA talk. Right? Can you at least give me that?

I'll take anything at this point. And if that something is a six-pack of preseason games tomorrow night, I'll gladly take it and RUN.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Welcome back, NFL. Let's get this preseason started so we can get through it as quickly as possible and get to the real thing.

Welcome to a Hump Day Nightcaps — the one where new Dallas Cowboys wife, Haley Cavinder (Ferguson), fires back at an internet troll who took a nasty little shot at her earlier this week.

This is what training camp is for, folks. Everyone is working out the kinks right now.

What else? I've got the wokes getting MAD MAD at Pat McAfee for attending a high school sporting event with President Donald Trump, Ryan Clark looking like an absolute clown after attacking Sophie Cunningham and Seahawks coach Mike McDonald going scorched earth on a player who breathed on Sam Darnold during practice.

No. 1 rule of training camp, folks. Don't touch the quarterback! Frankly, that's pretty much the No. 1 in games at this point.

OK, grab you a filet mignon for National Filet Mignon Day and settle in for a Hump Day 'Cap!

Can't believe it's been a full year since last year's NFMD! Time flies. I went back and looked at my Mount Rushmore of Steaks from last year's class, and I think I'd like to amend it today:

1. Ribeye (this one hasn't changed)

2. Filet (neither has this one)

3. Strip (left this one out last year)

4. Standing Rib Roast! (Also left this one out)

Nothing beats a Ribeye steak. I'll die on this hill. My wife is a strip steak truther because she claims the ribeyes are too fatty. Hogwash. The fat is the best part of a well-cooked ribeye.

Yes, I realize a rib roast is essentially a ribeye, but it tastes completely different to me. I did one on the smoker last Christmas Eve, and it was some of my finest work.

Pro tip: Get you a standing rib roast (or strip) when they're on sale at the Publix and have the butcher cut them for you. Vacuum seal them up and throw them in the freezer for a later date. You're welcome!

PAT MCAFEE ATTENDS SPORTING EVENT WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP WEARING JEANS AND A BACKWARDS CAP

OK, let's get this class started with new Dallas Cowboys WAG Haley Cavinder, wife of star TE Jake Ferguson, taking on an internet troll earlier this week:

"I posted this picture of me and my husband last Saturday and I was getting tagged on X because this man decided to comment on my looks and my smile," she said before dropping an 'F-U' on Teddy2steppin.

"I thought my smile looked good ... F–k you! Let me go practice my smile more for you."

Get him, Haley! Don't bend the knee to the #TROLLS! It's a tough life being a Dallas Cowboys WAG. Haley's in training camp right now, just as much as the players are.

She'll have the rust knocked off and be ready to roll when Sept. 13 rolls around and we're all forced to watch the 27th straight season of Giants-Cowboys opening up the Sunday Night Football schedule.

Can't wait.

Speaking of internet trolls, let's head back to X and see how folks are handling Pat McAfee's big night with Donald Trump at the Patriot Games:

I could go on and on. It's a cesspool over on Elon's app right now. People are FURIOUS with Pat McAfee today because he — checks notes — sat with the President of the United States at a high school sporting event?

Incredible. It really is amazing what these people get mad about. But yeah, let's go ahead and cancel Pat McAfee because he sat with Trump at a high school sporting event — which was on ABC/ESPN!

Surely the #MOB has this same energy for everyone, right?

Alllllllllllrighty then! Moving on ...

Let's rapid-fire this Hump Day class into a big Hump Day night. First up? Speaking of ESPNers, anyone see the absolute nonsense Ryan Clark spewed on his podcast yesterday?

Spoiler alert: He's not a Sophie Cunningham fan! Shocking, I know.

ANTI-CAITLIN CLARK ESPN PUNDIT TRIES JUSTIFYING CLAIM THAT CLARK ISN'T AMONG THE BEST GUARDS IN WNBA

"Divisive gossip from a 9-point scorer gets more attention than the league’s best teams and players," Clark tweeted Tuesday while also pushing a clip of his podcast further calling out Cunningham.

Without ever mentioning her name, of course.

"We're seeing players who don't even average 10 points a game, and that's who's on your networks and TVs, answering questions and starting back and forths about things that aren't basketball," he continued.

"To me, it's about pushing the right things. Talking about the right things. Making sure the right things are at the forefront of people's mind."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Clark also went on to list all the great WNBA players at the moment that we should instead be focusing on, and included Caitlin Clark ... with a caveat:

"It can be different ways, right? She can be one of the faces of the league, but you can acknowledge that she still has to get better at basketball."

Amazing. Ryan HATES Sophie and Caitlin. Hates, hates, HATES them. The best part?

Sophie was the best player on the court in last night's win over New York, going 4 of 5 from the field (all three-pointers) and finishing with a +/- of +17 — the best of any player who played.

But yeah, she's just a divisive gossiper who had the audacity to say that ... she wants to protect little girls in locker rooms.

Disgusting!

These people are just the best. The gift that keeps on giving. What a blessing.

OK, that's it for today. Good Hump Day, everyone.

Here's Seahawks coach Mike McDonald losing his you-know-what on a player that got a little too close to Sam Darnold during practice.

Not tolerated, clearly.

Best steak? Email me at Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

item.title: Former SPLC official arrested as feds expand case over alleged $4M scheme involving extremist groups
item.description: The Southern Poverty Law Center allegedly funneled $4.1 million in donor funds to extremists for KKK robes, cross burnings and member recruitment.
item.content:encoded:
A former top Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) official was arrested on charges Wednesday as federal prosecutors unveiled sweeping new allegations that donated money was allegedly secretly funneled to extremists and used for activities including recruiting members, staging rallies and buying materials for Ku Klux Klan robes and cross burnings.

Heidi Beirich, 59, of Palm Springs, California, was charged alongside the SPLC with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and conspiracy to submit false statements to a federally insured bank.

The second superseding indictment also charges Beirich with a conspiracy to commit concealed money laundering. Beirich was served with an arrest warrant Wednesday morning, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Alabama.

Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed the arrest during a news conference Wednesday in Washington, D.C., and said the federal investigation remains ongoing.

FIRST ON FOX: SPLC'S TAX-EXEMPT STATUS UNDER THREAT AFTER FIERY CAPITOL HILL HEARING

"I think, as alleged in the indictment, this individual participated in the scheme as alleged," Blanche said. "I believe she was part of the effort to open bank accounts and complete fictitious companies names and make payments that to individuals for reasons that were not, that were not accurate as described."

FBI Director Kash Patel also weighed in on the news via X, writing that Beirich was at the "center" of the bureau's ongoing investigation.

"As alleged, Heidi Beirich was at the center of our ongoing investigation into SPLC and their previously alleged criminal activity - where SPLC knowingly misled donors, who believed their money was being used to dismantle violent extremist organizations - when in fact, part of those donations were instead being used to pay senior leadership within those extremist groups," Patel wrote.

The 26-page indictment obtained by Fox News Digital alleges the SPLC secretly funneled at least $4.1 million in tax-exempt donor funds between 2007 and 2023 through bank accounts supposedly belonging to businesses unaffiliated with the organization. Prosecutors allege the money paid "field sources" who were leading or affiliated with violent extremist organizations.

Prosecutors allege donor money was used to attend and host extremist rallies, recruit members, grow and create extremist chapters, publish extremist literature and buy materials for KKK robes, hoods and cross burnings. The indictment also alleges two KKK members who wanted out of the movement were encouraged by the SPLC to remain and offered monthly payments and expenses.

One of the most explosive allegations centers on a source identified as "F-9," whom prosecutors say infiltrated the neo-Nazi National Alliance and received more than $1.2 million from the SPLC during the period covered by the indictment. Prosecutors allege Beirich oversaw payments to F-9 while also having a romantic relationship with him, with the pair sharing a home and two bank accounts.

FIRST ON FOX: SPLC’S LEGAL WOES GROW AS JIM JORDAN FIRES LATEST SALVO AT LEFT-WING GROUP

Between 2015 and 2021, approximately $140,000 in donor money flowed from the SPLC's operating account through a "Tech Writers" account and ultimately into joint bank accounts held by Beirich and F-9, prosecutors allege. The indictment says the money accounted for approximately 66% of all funds deposited into their joint accounts and alleges Beirich used donor money to pay the couple's personal living expenses.

The indictment also alleges F-9 broke into an extremist organization's headquarters in 2014 and stole approximately 25 boxes of documents. Prosecutors allege that, with Beirich's knowledge, donor money was used to copy the stolen material before it was returned and that Beirich used the copies as the basis for an SPLC "Hatewatch" story. The indictment alleges Beirich later paid another source approximately $6,000 in donor money to then falsely take responsibility for the burglary.

"The indictment unsealed today reflects the continued work of federal investigators and prosecutors in examining this alleged scheme," U.S. Attorney Thomas Govan said. "We look forward to presenting the evidence in court and allowing the judicial process to determine the facts and the defendants’ responsibility for the alleged crimes."

Beirich is expected in federal court in Riverside, Calif., Wednesday afternoon at 2:00 p.m. PT, sources tell Fox News.

The SPLC has previously denied wrongdoing and moved to dismiss the federal case. An indictment contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

"Taking on violent hate and extremist groups is among the most dangerous work there is, and we believe it is also among the most important work we do. The actions taken by the DOJ will not shake our resolve," the SPLC said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "We remain steadfast in our fight for justice and in our commitment to ensuring the promise of the Civil Rights movement becomes a reality for all. We are confident in our position and look forward to presenting the evidence and making our case in court."

Fox News Digital's Asra Nomani, and Fox News' David Spunt and Bill Mears contributed to this report.

item.title: ICE asks Kentucky officials to hold previously deported man charged with rape while working as landlord
item.description: ICE lodged an immigration detainer in Louisville after Rolando Cenobio Vasquez was charged with rape and human trafficking of a 15-year-old girl.
item.content:encoded:
Federal immigration officials are asking a Kentucky jail to hold an illegal immigrant charged with rape, human trafficking and sexual abuse while working as a landlord so he can be taken into custody for deportation proceedings.

Rolando Cenobio Vasquez, a Mexican citizen, was arrested July 29 by Louisville police, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) said.

Vasquez had been renting out a room to a mother and her 15-year-old daughter when he began abusing the teenager in December 2025, authorities said.

ICE DETAINS ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT ACCUSED OF SEXUALLY ASSAULTING MINOR AFTER HOSPITAL PARKING LOT BIRTH

"ICE has lodged a detainer asking officials in Louisville, Kentucky, to not release this criminal from jail and to hand him over to ICE custody so he can be removed from our country," a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said.

Vasquez allegedly threatened the mother and child but occasionally offered the teenager money to keep quiet about the sexual abuse, authorities said.

He was charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sodomy, human trafficking, promoting human trafficking with a victim under 18 and sexual abuse.

Vasquez's criminal history includes a prior conviction for driving under the influence of liquor. ICE lodged a detainer with the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections the same day he was arrested.

WATCH: DEM DEMANDS 'ONE CASE' WHERE SANCTUARY CITIES DIDN'T TURN OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS; DHS PROVIDES LIST

Vasquez initially entered the United States illegally in August 2013 through Texas, DHS said. He was arrested by the U.S. Border Patrol and deported.

It was not clear when he illegally reentered the U.S., according to DHS.

Louisville is not a sanctuary jurisdiction. In July 2025, the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections agreed to follow a federal law requiring inmates in custody be held for up to 48 hours on what are called immigration detainers.

item.title: Molly Sims calls out Hollywood for lying about beauty secrets
item.description: Molly Sims slammed Hollywood's fake beauty secrets, saying stars lie about drinking water and sleep when facelifts and peptides tell the real story.
item.content:encoded:
Molly Sims is getting real about Hollywood spewing fake beauty secrets.

During a recent interview with US Magazine, the 53-year-old model slammed people in Hollywood for lying about how they maintain their camera-ready look.

"Early on, other models would help you. Like, 'I’m getting shots in my a--,' or 'I’m only going to drink grapefruit juice,'" she explained. "Hollywood people would say, 'I just drink a lot of water, and I slept eight hours.' I’m like, 'No, you f---ing didn’t.'"

She went on to say that while out to dinner with a group of girlfriends recently, "all we did was talk about everybody’s facelift."

MARTHA STEWART GETS CANDID ABOUT PLASTIC SURGERY, DATING AS SHE TURNS 85

"We’re like, 'She looks amazing. She did the upper lip, the lower. She did the CO2,'" she said. "It’s refreshing for a woman in Kentucky or Ohio to know that it’s not just drinking water and getting a good night’s sleep. You too can be on the peptide."

The model also spoke about how her approach to her appearance has evolved from her early days in the modeling industry to now, as a woman in her 50s.

Sims recalled coming into the industry "during a difficult era called 'heroin chic,'" saying the expectation was to be "about 20 pounds underweight and very goth," noting the scrutiny she received was "devastating."

"I went from Vanderbilt with my sorority sisters, where you’re dipping your fries in a Wendy’s Frosty and you think nothing of it," she said. "I was from a completely different world, and also the business had changed. [The] beautiful, normal body weight was not [in style] when I entered, and it gave me a lot of pause and a lot of tears."

Nowadays, when Sims works out, her ultimate goal is not to look younger, but "to look the best I can at every age," saying, "I don't want to be skinny; I want to be healthy."

Sims left Vanderbilt University in the early 1990s to pursue modeling, and broke through into mainstream recognition when she posed for the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue in 2000, returning to the magazine in 2001, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2020 and 2024.

She made her most recent appearance in the magazine in 2026, posing in a number of two-piece sets, including orange, pink and red string bikinis.

"If only I could tell the 20-something version of me shooting her first @si_swimsuit issue that she’d still be here at 52… feeling more beautiful and confident in her skin than ever before 🥹Thank you @mj_day and my entire SI family!!! ❤️" she shared on Instagram alongside photos from the magazine.
